Day by day

Loading…

Mon 12 OctRome

Land in Rome

Leonardo Express from FCO (€14, 32 min) to Termini. Drop bags, then walk — don’t nap. Aperitivo in Monti, early night. Borghese is shut Mondays, so don’t plan it today.

Tue 13 OctRome

Ancient Rome

Colosseum on your booked slot (go 8:30), then the Forum and up Palatine Hill — same ticket, 24 hours. Lunch at Supplizio. Afternoon: San Clemente’s three stacked churches. Evening: Trevi after 10pm, free and half empty.

Wed 14 OctRome

The Vatican

Museums early on your booked slot, finish at the Sistine Chapel, then St Peter’s. Lunch at Pizzarium, five minutes from the exit. Heads up: Wednesday is the papal audience — St Peter’s Square is closed off much of the morning. Museums first, Basilica after 1pm.

Thu 15 OctRome

Baroque and Caravaggio

Borghese Gallery on your timed slot — Bernini’s sculptures, the best two hours in Rome. Walk back through the gardens. Afternoon: Pantheon, San Luigi dei Francesi for the Caravaggios (shut 12:45–14:30), Santa Maria sopra Minerva. Dinner in Trastevere.

Fri 16 OctSorrento

Rome to Sorrento

Morning train to Naples (1h10, pre-booked), then Campania Express to Sorrento (€15, seat and luggage space). Afternoon: settle in, down to Marina Grande, sunset from the Villa Comunale gardens.

Sat 17 OctSorrento

Pompeii

Early train to Pompei Scavi (~30 min, station 100 m from the gate). Your 9am slot — carry your passport, the ticket is named. Allow 4–6 hours; it is a whole city with almost no shade. Back for a late lunch and a swim if the sun holds.

Sun 18 OctSorrento

Your extra Sorrento day

The day the longer stay buys you. Pick one: Herculaneum (€16 — smaller than Pompeii but far better preserved, wooden doors and upper floors still standing), Vesuvius to walk the crater rim (€10 + bus), or Naples for the Veiled Christ, Caravaggio at Pio Monte, and pizza at Da Michele. Or do none of it and take the boat along the coast.

Mon 19 OctTropea

Sorrento to Tropea

A long one, ~6–7 h. Circumvesuviana to Naples, then train to Lamezia Terme, then the regional down to Tropea. Book the Naples–Lamezia leg early — it is €20–45 in advance and much more on the day. Eat properly before the last leg.

Tue 20 OctTropea

The Aeolian Islands — Stromboli

Book this before anything else. Leaves Tropea 14:00, back ~22:30: three and a half hours ashore on Stromboli, then after dark the boat rounds the Sciara del Fuoco to watch lava run into the sea. €70 direct at tropea.biz. The season ends 24 October, so this is one of the last sailings. Take a jacket.

Wed 21 OctTropea

Tropea

Slow day. Santa Maria dell’Isola late afternoon when the light is good (church free, rooftop €3). The belvederes along Corso Vittorio Emanuele. White-sand beaches, free and empty, sea still ~22°C. Gelato at Tonino — the Tropea red onion flavour is not a joke. (If the boat did not run yesterday, today is your second chance.)

Thu 22 OctCefalù

Tropea to Cefalù — your train rides a ferry

Regional to Villa San Giovanni, then InterCity 723 (~14:25): the carriages are loaded onto a ferry and you cross the Strait of Messina by sea. Stay in your seat or go up on deck and watch Sicily arrive. Cefalù 18:24, so it is dark when you land — drop the bag and go straight to dinner. Book La Brace ahead.

Fri 23 OctPalermo

Cefalù, then on to Palermo

La Rocca first thing — 45–60 min of steps, closed shoes required, and the whole coast from the top. Then the Duomo’s Pantocrator mosaic and the medieval washhouse. The €10 SIBAC pass covers the rock, the museum and three more. Lunch, a last swim off the town beach, then the evening train to Palermo (~1 h, €7.50).

Sat 24 OctPalermo

Palermo proper

La Martorana first (€2, mornings only, and shut Mondays — so it has to be today). The best mosaics-per-euro in Sicily; San Cataldo next door. Then Cappella Palatina (€19, last entry 15:45) and the Cathedral rooftops. Afternoon: Palazzo Abatellis or Palazzo Butera in the Kalsa, both shut tomorrow’s alternative day. Street food all the way through: panelle, sfincione, arancine.

Sun 25 OctPalermo

Mondello, and Rigoletto

Clocks went back overnight — an hour in hand, but dark by six from now on. Sunday is Palermo’s worst day for monuments, so go to the sea instead. Bus 812 up Monte Pellegrino for the view, then 806 out to Mondello: a curve of white sand under the mountain with a Liberty-style pavilion on stilts. Sea is ~22°C. Then the night of the trip: Verdi’s Rigoletto at the Teatro Massimo, with Ludovic Tézier in the title role. Seats from €27.

Mon 26 OctPalermo

Monreale and the Catacombs

The right day for this, because everything else is shut on a Monday. Capuchin Catacombs at 09:00 — 8,000 mummified Palermitans still in their clothes; it closes 12:30–15:00, so go first. Then walk to Piazza Indipendenza and take bus 389 up to Monreale: 6,500 m² of gold mosaic, the whole Bible floor to ceiling. Cathedral before 13:00, cloister after. Buy the €3.50 AMAT day ticket — four buses today.

Tue 27 OctFavignana

Palermo to Favignana

Segesta bus to Trapani (€9.60, 2 h) from Piazzetta Cairoli right behind Palermo Centrale — not the train, that line has been shut since 2013 and the detour takes five hours. The bus drops you at Trapani port, which is where the hydrofoils go from. Then ~30 minutes across to Favignana. Hire a bike when you land.

Wed 28 OctFavignana

Favignana by bike

The island is flat and about 9 km end to end, so a bike is genuinely all you need. Cala Rossa and Bue Marino are old tuff quarries the sea has flooded — sheer cut-stone walls dropping straight into turquoise. Cala Azzurra and Lido Burrone for actual sand.

Thu 29 OctFavignana

Favignana

The Florio tuna cannery tells the whole story of the island — this was one of the great tuna fisheries of the Mediterranean. Then the climb up to Santa Caterina fort for the view over both Favignana and Levanzo. Swim, eat tuna, do very little.

Fri 30 OctFavignana

Favignana — last full day

A boat around the island if one is running, or the short hop to Levanzo and its prehistoric cave paintings. Otherwise cycle somewhere you have not been and swim off the rocks. Last proper day of the trip — spend it slowly.

Sat 31 OctRome

Favignana to Rome

Ferry back to Trapani, then on to Rome. Take a morning sailing, not the last one — this is the leg with the most moving parts and it is the day before you fly home. Evening in Rome: last carbonara, and repack.

Sun 1 Nov→ home

Fly home

All Saints’ Day. The Vatican is closed, but state museums including the Colosseum are free this morning if you have hours to spare — crowded, though. Leonardo Express to FCO (€14, every 15 min); allow three hours. Sunday timetable, so leave a little extra.

What to book & when

🔴 Book NOW (late August)
  • All hotels — Favignana first (small island, few beds, and places start shutting for winter), then the 31 Oct Rome night (All Saints' long weekend, rates jump 10–25%).
  • Vatican Museums €25 — Book official Closed Sundays.
  • Borghese Gallery €18 — Book official Timed slots, closed Mondays.
  • Rome→Naples train 16 Oct €9–19 now — Trenitalia Italo (later: €40–55).
  • Naples→Lamezia Terme train 19 Oct €20–45 — Trenitalia
  • Flight back to Rome, 31 Oct €25–90 — from Trapani (TPS) if there is a flight that suits, otherwise Palermo (PMO). Skyscanner · Ryanair · ITA. Book early — this is the tightest link in the trip.
  • 🌋 Aeolian Islands day trip from Tropea €70 — Book direct Tue 20 or Wed 21 Oct — the season ends on the 24th, so you are catching the last week. Stromboli's lava after dark. Needs minimum numbers to run, so book early.
  • Cappella Sansevero, Naples €10 — Book official The Veiled Christ. Sells out fast.
  • Travel insurance A$350–700 — Fast Cover · Cover-More.
  • eSIM — Airalo Eurolink ≈ A$148.
  • Cards — Up Bank + Wise, 1–2 weeks to arrive.
🟠 September
  • ⏰ Colosseum — alarm for 12 Sept, 9:00am Italy (5pm AEST) €18 — Book official Releases exactly 30 days ahead; morning slots gone within hours. Want the underground? You need the €32 official guided visit — the plain ticket won't get you down there.
  • Pompeii €20 — Book official Named ticket, must match your passport. Book a 9am slot for 17 Oct.
  • Any tours you want — food tours, cooking classes and boat trips fill up; see each stop's "Experiences" list.
  • Palazzo Colonna (if you want it) — opens Fri & Sat mornings only; your only chances are 16 Oct, 30 Oct or 31 Oct.
🟡 1–2 weeks before each leg
  • Trapani → Favignana hydrofoil (28 Oct) and back (31 Oct) — Liberty Lines. Sailings thin out in late October, so check the timetable before you commit to a flight time on the 31st.
  • Re-verify IC 723 (Villa San Giovanni ~14:25 → Cefalù 18:24) on Trenitalia.
  • Message each hotel to confirm check-in and that they're open.
🟢 Buy on the day
  • SITA buses (tabacchi shops, NOT on board), Circumvesuviana, regional trains — validate paper tickets or it's a €100 fine.
  • La Rocca (€5 or the €10 SIBAC pass), Trevi (€2, free after 10pm), Capuchin Crypt in Rome (on-site only), Favignana bike hire.

Rome

12–16 Oct · 4 nights

Four days is enough for the big three plus real wandering. Mon–Fri means thinner crowds than a weekend. Nearly everything inside the walls is walkable — you'll use the metro maybe twice a day. City tax €4–6 per person per night on top of the room, usually cash at checkout.

Walking map

Everything here is walkable. The Vatican is the exception — take Metro A to Ottaviano (15 min from Termini).

arrivesightsstayeat & beach3′ = walking minutes

The big sights — prices & booking
Colosseum + Forum + Palatine — one ticket, all three, valid 24h. Book official (⏰ 12 Sept, 9am Italy). Go 8:30am or last slot 📍€18
Colosseum underground + arena — official 75-min guided visit. A guide is legally required for the tunnels; the standard ticket won't do it book€32
Vatican Museums + Sistine — book now. Closed Sun. Tue/Thu quietest 📍€25
Vatican Friday night opening — 19:00–23:00, same price, magical and half-empty. Season ends ~26 Oct, so Fri 16 Oct is your shot (it's your Sorrento travel day — only if you go late)€25
St Peter's Basilica — free. Before 8am or after 4pm. Dome climb €10 stairs / €15 lift. Shoulders + knees covered 📍free
Pantheon — buy at the door 📍€7
Borghese Gallery — Bernini's sculptures. Timed slot only, closed Mon 📍€18
Trevi Fountain — €2 daytime, free after 10pm and far better lit 📍€2/0
Catacombs — San Callisto (closed Wed) or San Sebastiano; guided tour included. Bus 118 📍€10
Your Paul churches — 📍 San Paolo Fuori le Mura (metro B, cloister €4); 📍 San Luigi dei Francesi — three Caravaggios, bring €1 coins for the lights, shut 12:45–14:30; 📍 Santa Maria sopra Minervafree
More Rome — the ones people miss
Basilica di San Clemente — three churches stacked on top of each other: 12th-century over 4th-century over a Roman house with a Mithras temple, an underground stream still running. 45 min, 200 m from the Colosseum. The best "layers of Rome" thing you can do 📍€10
Castel Sant'Angelo — Hadrian's tomb turned papal fortress; the ramparts have the best sunset view over the river 📍€16
Capuchin Crypt — chapels decorated with the bones of 3,700 friars. Genuinely startling. Tickets on-site only 📍€10
Baths of Caracalla — vast ruined imperial baths, walls still eight storeys high, almost nobody there 📍€8
Palazzo Doria Pamphilj — a still-private family palace; the audio guide is narrated by the prince who lives there. Or Palazzo Barberini (€12) for Caravaggio's Judith 📍€16
Centrale Montemartini — Roman marble gods posed against the turbines of a 1912 power station. Strange and wonderful, and empty 📍€7.50
Free and lovely — the Aventine Keyhole (St Peter's dome framed perfectly through a door), the orange garden next to it, Quartiere Coppedè's fairytale architecture 📍free
Experiences worth booking
  • Testaccio food tour + aperitivo €79 A$134Rome's real food neighbourhood — market stalls, supplì, cheese, wine. Trastevere farmers-market version €69. Book
  • Pasta-making class €85–130 A$145–221Make it, then sit down and eat it with wine. Small groups. Cookly · GetYourGuide
  • Three Tenors concert €25–35 A$43–60Opera arias and Neapolitan songs in a church on Via Nazionale, about an hour. Runs all autumn. Tickets
  • Appian Way by bike €15–25 A$26–43Original Roman paving, aqueducts, catacombs along the way. Go Sunday — the road closes to traffic. Hire
  • Villa Borghese rowboat €3–5 A$5–920 minutes rowing around a little temple on a lake. Absurdly cheap, absurdly romantic. Cash, no booking.
  • Ostia Antica €18 + €3 train A$36 totalRome's own Pompeii — a whole port city, half an hour away, a fraction of the crowds. Closed Mondays.
  • Tivoli — Villa d'Este €12 + €8 train A$34 totalA Renaissance garden of five hundred fountains, all gravity-fed. Half a day.
Where to stay — 10 options by price

Cheap · €45–90

  • The Beehive €45–80 BookBeloved indie guesthouse 300 m from Termini, garden café. Dorms from €22.
  • Hotel Nardizzi Americana 3★ €73–95 BookRooftop terrace, midway between Termini and Trevi. Best value in the guide.
  • Relais Le Clarisse 3★ €85–115 BookA 17th-century convent in Trastevere; rooms around a walled garden, quiet despite the nightlife.

Comfortable · €90–120

  • Hotel Centro Cavour 3★ €105–120 BookIn Monti, 10 min walk to the Colosseum, free buffet breakfast. 8.9/10 from 2,800+ reviews.
  • Hotel Sonya 3★ €83–110 BookOpposite the Opera House, two minutes from Termini — easy for the Naples train.
  • Blue Hostel €90–110 BookA boutique B&B despite the name — Monti, 17th-century building, en-suite doubles.
  • Hotel Alimandi Vaticano 3★ €115–140 BookLiterally across the road from the Vatican Museums entrance. Ask for a rear room — street noise.

Treat yourself · €130–190

  • Hotel Diana Roof Garden 4★ €140–180 BookBreakfast on a roof garden over the Roman skyline, 200 m from Termini. The best-connected splurge.
  • Hotel Modigliani 4★ €130–165 BookFamily-owned, 28 rooms near the Spanish Steps, with a big private garden hidden inside the block.
  • Trilussa Palace 4★ €160–190 BookTrastevere, rooftop bar on the 8th floor, private spa suites. The one for the last two nights.
Eat & drink

Cheap & classic

  • Supplizio €3–4 📍The best supplì in Rome — fried rice balls with molten mozzarella inside. Two is lunch.
  • Trapizzino €4–5 📍A pizza pocket filled with Roman stews — chicken cacciatora, oxtail. Invented in Testaccio.
  • Pizzarium Bonci €5–7 📍Pizza by weight, five minutes from the Vatican Museums exit. Your Vatican-day lunch, sorted.
  • Otaleg / Giolitti €3–5 📍Gelato. Otaleg in Trastevere is the connoisseur's pick; Giolitti near the Pantheon is the institution.

Sit-down dinner

  • Da Enzo al 29 €10–14 a plate 📍Tiny Trastevere trattoria, the benchmark for carbonara and cacio e pepe. No bookings for small tables — queue before 7pm.
  • Armando al Pantheon €35–45pp 📍Same family since 1961, right by the Pantheon, and somehow still not a tourist trap. Book ahead.
  • Roscioli €40–55pp 📍Deli-counter-meets-wine-bar. Famous carbonara, extraordinary cheese and cured meat. Book well ahead.

Espresso standing at the bar €1.20–1.50 — sitting down costs triple. Lunch menù del giorno is 30–40% cheaper than the same food at dinner.

Getting in & around

FCO airport → city €14Leonardo Express, 32 min nonstop to Termini, every 15 min. Taxi is a fixed €55 — only white cars marked "Roma Capitale", never the Fiumicino-plated ones.

Around town €1.50Single ticket, 100 minutes. Tap your card straight on the metro gates. Honestly, you'll walk most of it.

16 Oct → Sorrento €9–19 + €5–15Frecciarossa or Italo to Naples (1h10), then Circumvesuviana (€5, 70 min, hold your bag) or Campania Express (€15, guaranteed seat and luggage space).

Sorrento

16–19 Oct · 3 nights

A cliff-top town facing Vesuvius across the bay, and the perfect base — Pompeii, Herculaneum, Vesuvius and Naples are all on one train line. With three nights you get Pompeii and a proper second day, instead of having to choose.

Walking map

A compact grid on a cliff. Everything below is 15 minutes or less from Piazza Tasso.

arrivesightsstayeat & beach3′ = walking minutes

Pompeii — the big one
Entry, "Pompeii Express" — book official. Named ticket — carry your passport. Timed slots, 20,000/day cap; book a 9am slot by late Sept 📍€20
"Pompeii+" — adds the Villa of the Mysteries and its fresco cycle, the best-preserved Roman painting anywhere. Worth the extra €5€25
Official 1.5-hour guided tour on top of entry — good value versus €35–55 private tours+€8
Train from Sorrento to "Pompei Scavi – Villa dei Misteri", ~30 min, station is 100 m from the gate~€3

Open 9:00–19:30, last entry 17:30. Allow 4–6 hours — it's a whole city, 66 hectares, with almost no shade. Proper shoes, hat, water (there are free ancient fountains to refill at). Bags bigger than 30×30×15 cm go in the cloakroom.

Day trips from Sorrento
Naples — train to Garibaldi (~70 min). Walk Spaccanapoli and Via dei Tribunali, free. Watch your bag near the station 📍€5
Cappella Sansevero, Naples — the Veiled Christ: one block of marble carved to look like wet cloth over a body. Book ahead, it sells out 📍€10
MANN museum, Naples — where the actual Pompeii mosaics and frescoes live. Closed Tuesdays 📍€20
Pio Monte della Misericordia, Naples — Caravaggio's Seven Works of Mercy, still hanging in the chapel it was painted for. Two minutes from Sansevero 📍€10
Herculaneum — smaller than Pompeii but far better preserved: wooden doors, upper floors, carbonised furniture. Fewer people too. Check the train stops at Ercolano Scavi 📍€16
Mount Vesuvius crater — walk to the rim and look in. DIY: train to Pompeii + EAV bus 808 (€5.40 return) + entry. Book a timed slot 📍€10
Napoli Sotterranea — 40 m under the city: Greek aqueduct, WWII shelter, a hidden Roman theatre. Guided, ~90 min 📍€10–15
In Sorrento itself — free & cheap
  • Vallone dei Mulini — a 900-year-old flour mill abandoned in a gorge, now swallowed by ferns. Visible from the street off Piazza Tasso. Free, 5 minutes, best photo in town. 📍
  • Marina Grande — the fishing village below the cliffs, with the best seafood in town at half the Piazza Tasso price. 10 min downhill. 📍
  • Bagni della Regina Giovanna — a natural sea pool inside a ruined Roman villa, 30–40 min walk west. Free, and still swimmable in October. 📍
  • Villa Comunale gardens at sunset — Vesuvius going pink across the water. Free.
Experiences worth booking
  • Lemon grove & limoncello tour €40–65 A$68–110Walk a working grove, see it made, taste it. The "Nonno Mario" version (€65) includes food. Free tastings at I Giardini di Cataldo if you'd rather not pay.
  • Cooking class in a local's home €95–125 A$162–213Pasta and tiramisù, 3 hours, then you eat it. The "Cesarina" home-cooking network is the standout. Book
  • Pizza-making class €55–75 A$94–128Shorter and cheaper — dough to wood-fired oven in about 90 minutes, wine included.
  • Boat trip to Capri €90–169 A$153–287Small wooden gozzo, max 12 people, swim stops, a few hours ashore. Lovely — but you're staying on Capri anyway, so maybe skip.
  • Naples street-food tour €49 A$83Pizza a portafoglio, sfogliatella, mozzarella, cuoppo — 2–3 hours with someone who knows which door to knock on.
  • Sorrento Musei 3-museum pass €31 A$53Correale decorative arts + its clifftop garden, the inlaid-woodwork museum, and Sorrento Experience. Closed Mondays.

Eat & drink

In Sorrento

  • Trattoria da Emilia €10–14 📍Down at Marina Grande since 1947. Gnocchi alla sorrentina the way it's supposed to be.
  • Da Filippo €25–35pp 📍Family-run with a garden terrace and a wood oven. The nice-dinner option.

In Naples

  • L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele €6.50 📍Two pizzas on the menu, both perfect, since 1870. Take a ticket and wait.
  • Gino Sorbillo €5.50 📍The other titan, on Via dei Tribunali. Go early or expect a queue.
  • Attanasio €2 📍Hot sfogliatella two minutes from the station. Time your train around it.

Tropea

19–22 Oct · 3 nights

A town on a cliff above white-sand beaches, with a monastery on a rock in the sea below it. This is where the trip slows down — Calabria gets a fraction of the visitors the Amalfi Coast does, prices drop by half, and almost everyone you meet will be Italian. Three nights of not much, deliberately.

Walking map

The old town sits 50 m up on a cliff; the beach and the rock are down a long staircase.

arrivesightsstayeat & beach3′ = walking minutes

Getting there — 19 Oct (a long one, ~6–7 h)

1 · Sorrento → Naples €5–15Circumvesuviana (~70 min) or the Campania Express with a guaranteed seat. Go early — you have a long day.

2 · Train Naples → Lamezia Terme €20–45Frecciarossa ~3 h or InterCity ~4 h down the coast. Book now while it is cheap.

3 · Regional to Tropea €5.30About an hour, roughly 9 a day, buy on the app that morning. The direct Naples–Tropea train only runs in summer.

Eat before the last legLamezia station is not somewhere you want to be hungry. Grab something in Naples or on the Frecciarossa.

⚠ Book this before anything else: the Aeolian Islands The 2026 season ends on Saturday 24 October, and you are here for the last week of it — sailings run on Tuesday 20 and Wednesday 21 October. Boats run from Tropea port to Stromboli, where you watch the volcano's lava run down the Sciara del Fuoco into the sea after dark. €70 all in (A$119) booked direct at tropea.biz — resellers charge €94–101 for the identical trip. Low-season sailings need minimum numbers, so book early or it may not run.
The Aeolian Islands — your two chances
  • Tue 20 Oct — Stromboli by Night €70 ← the pickLeaves Tropea 14:00, back ~22:30. Three and a half hours ashore on Stromboli, then the boat circles round after dark to watch lava run down the Sciara del Fuoco into the sea.
  • Wed 21 Oct — Vulcano, Lipari & Stromboli by day €7007:45 to ~18:45, a full twelve hours. You don't land on Stromboli on this one — you see the Sciara from the sea. Also your fallback if Tuesday is cancelled.

Book direct at tropea.biz — €70 including the landing tax, versus €94–101 through resellers. Low-season sailings need minimum numbers, so book early. Free cancellation with 48 hours' notice, and weather cancellations are rebooked without penalty.

In and around Tropea
  • Santa Maria dell'Isola — a Benedictine sanctuary on its own rock, reached by steps cut into the stone. Church free, the garden and rooftop €3. Go late afternoon. 📍
  • The belvederes along Corso Vittorio Emanuele — the old town sits 50 m up on a cliff and every few hundred metres there's a balcony over the sea. Free, best an hour before sunset.
  • The beaches — white sand, turquoise water, empty in late October. Clubs shut, sand free, sea ~22.8°C.
  • Scilla €5.40 — 1h05 by direct train, seven a day. Chianalea is a fishing village where the houses stand in the water and the lanes are one person wide. The best day trip from here. 📍
  • Vibo Valentia €2.70 + €1.80 bus — train to Vibo Marina then the shuttle up the hill. The Norman castle holds the archaeological museum (€5). Note the town is 470 m up — you need that bus, and it doesn't run Sundays.
  • Pizzo for the tartufo — the ice-cream bomb was invented here and Bar Ercole still makes the original (€5–7). 📍
  • Boat along the Costa degli Dei €35–45 — Capitan Paolo (€39.90) or SeeTropea (€45), around 3 hours with swim stops and snorkelling. Season officially runs to end of October but operators thin out fast — ask at the port when you arrive.
Food & wine experiences — book direct, save a lot
ℹ Skip the booking sites here CST Tropea sells the same tours on GetYourGuide for €24–32 more per person than on their own site. Book at csttropea.it — two people doing two tours saves about €100.
  • Street food walking tour €75 direct A$1283 hours, daily at 17:30 — the cathedral and the viewpoints, then red onion done several ways, local cheeses and an aperitif. €99 on GetYourGuide for the same thing.
  • Wine & olive oil tasting €43 direct A$73Organic winery at Brattirò, 5 km out: six wines, cheese, salami, honey, a vineyard walk. Runs Thursday afternoons — fits 22 Oct. €75 on the booking sites.
  • Olive oil experience €45 A$77Walk the grove, see the mill, taste properly. Friday afternoons — fits 23 Oct. Late October is the start of the real olive harvest, so ask whether the mill will be running.
  • Cooking class "I Segreti" €85 A$145Three hours at a vineyard making fileja pasta and a Tropea onion dish, then lunch with wine. Mondays and Thursdays — fits 22 Oct.
  • Cheaper cooking class €49–56 A$83–95Accademia di Chef at Spilinga — fresh pasta, local buffet, unlimited wine. The best-value class of the trip.
  • 'Nduja factory & onion farm €60–90 A$102–153Out to Spilinga where 'nduja actually comes from. The €60 version includes a three-course lunch.
  • In-town wine tasting €45 A$77Mazzola Drink & Wine — one hour, three Calabrian wines with a sommelier, plus a board of 'nduja and cheese. Walkable, no car, low commitment.
⚠ Capo Vaticano & getting around — read this

Capo Vaticano is not reachable by public transport on your dates. The Tropea–Capo Vaticano shuttle only runs 5 June–10 September, so it's been stopped six weeks by the time you arrive. The train to Ricadi is cheap (€1.40, 9 min) but leaves you ~3 km from the lighthouse with no onward bus.

  • Taxi — about €27–36 each way, so €55–75 return with waiting.
  • Hire a car for a day or two — Rent Car Tropea on Via Annunziata does a Fiat Panda from €40–50/day (0963 666033). Lamezia airport is half that but costs you an hour of train each way. One day of hire costs less than two taxi runs and also unlocks Spilinga and the inland villages.
  • Or just see it from the water — every Costa degli Dei boat tour rounds Capo Vaticano. Cheaper, and arguably the better view.
ℹ Your travel day is now a Thursday Which is good news — Calabrian regional trains thin right out at weekends, and the old plan had you leaving on a Sunday. Thursday has the full timetable.
Where to stay — 7 options by price

Live rates for 22–25 Oct. Tropea is not a seasonal problem — 28 hotels showed availability — but eight four-star places are already sold out or closed, so don't leave it.

Cheap · €60–90

  • Donnaciccina €60–80 BookA B&B in a restored old-town palazzo down an alley. One of the best-rated places in town.
  • La Porta del Mare €83 Book8.8/10 from 755 reviews, private beach area, free parking right outside, 150 m from the sand.

Comfortable · €98–110

  • Mediterranean Boutique Hotel 3★ €98 Book8.8/10 from 1,657 reviews — the biggest track record in Tropea. Beachfront with a private beach, restaurant, free parking.
  • Bonsai €105 Book9.2/10 "Superb". Private stair access down to the beach, breakfast and parking included, free cancellation to 22 Sept. The pick. No lift.
  • Aether Suites / Atlantide Suites €85–110 Book9.4 and 9.5 rated, both central and walkable.

Treat yourself · €145–186

  • Tropis Hotel 4★ €145 (€170 sea view) BookTwo pools, a spa, gym and two restaurants — and still only 350 m from the historic centre. Best facilities per euro on the trip.
  • Ananea Tropea Yachting Resort 5★ €186 Book9.0/10, newly renovated marina-front design hotel with a private beach and pool. Sits below the old town, so it's a stair climb up into town.
Eat & drink — 'nduja country

Don't miss

  • Gelati Tonino €3–5 📍Sixty-odd flavours including Tropea red onion and 'nduja gelato. Sounds wrong, tastes remarkable. Trust it.
  • Livasì Food & Store €8–15 📍Boards of 'nduja, pecorino and Calabrian salumi with a glass of local red.

Dinner — all three confirmed taking bookings on your dates

  • 3Nodi ~€32pp 📍9.1/10 from 1,164 diners — the most-reviewed restaurant in town. Down on the north pier. Salt cod in a golden crust with caramelised Tropea onion (€20), slow-cooked octopus on Sila potato cream (€22). Lunch and dinner.
  • Cinque Sensi ~€35pp 📍9.4/10, the highest-rated in Tropea. Contemporary Calabrian on a small old-town patio — fileja with red onion and 'nduja (€20), scorpionfish ragù (€24). Thu–Sat dinner only, so it fits your 22–24 Oct exactly.
  • Nonna Rosa Bistrot ~€30pp 📍9.2/10. Fresh-tuna carbonara (€16), amberjack risotto (€18). Old town, dinner from 19:00, and the most romantic of the three.

All three take bookings on TheFork — worth doing, they're small. Backups: Villa Adua, Da Cecè, REM Tropea Vecchia.

Shops here still close 1–4pm. Plan around it — and don't turn up for dinner before 8pm, you'll be alone.

José Luiz / Wikimedia · CC BY-SA 4.0 · more photos of Cefalù

Cefalù

22–23 Oct · 1 night

Medieval lanes running down to a sandy beach, a vast rock behind the town, and a Norman cathedral with a gold mosaic Christ that has been looking down since 1131. One night, but you get a decent day and a half out of it: you arrive at dusk on Thursday, have all of Friday, then take an evening train on to Palermo. Enough for the cathedral, the rock and a swim — Palermo gets its own base next, so nothing here needs day-tripping.

Walking map

Old town between the rock and the sea. Nothing is more than ten minutes from anything else.

arrivesightsstayeat & beach3′ = walking minutes

Getting there — 25 Oct (your train rides a ferry)

1 · Regional train to Villa San Giovanni ~€61h15–1h45 direct from Tropea, down to the toe of Italy.

2 · InterCity 723 to Cefalù €13–20Departs ~14:25. Here's the good bit: the whole train is shunted onto a ferry to cross the Strait of Messina. You can stay in your seat or go up on deck and watch Sicily arrive. Cefalù at 18:24. Book on Trenitalia — and re-check the time a month out.

DIY alternative ~€18–20Caronte foot ferry across (€2.50, every 40 min), walk 10 min to Messina Centrale, then a train along the coast. Same money, more flexible, less fun.

Do in Cefalù
✓ Buy the SIBAC combined ticket — €10 Covers La Rocca, the Mandralisca Museum, the Teatro Cicero, the Roman road site and the medieval washhouse, valid five days. The first two alone are €13 separately. Sold at the Rocca entrance, the museum, the station info desk and the visitor centre on Corso Ruggero.
The Duomo — UNESCO Arab-Norman cathedral. The apse mosaic of Christ Pantocrator is nine centuries old and still the best thing in Sicily. Nave free; the "red route" adds the rooftops, cloister and treasury (€13), or just the towers and roofs for €10 site 📍free
La Rocca — 45–60 minutes of steps up the rock behind town to the ruined Temple of Diana and a view along the whole coast. Closed shoes required, last entry well before dusk. Go in the morning 📍€5
Mandralisca Museum — for one painting: Antonello da Messina's Portrait of an Unknown Sailor, smirking at you from 1465. Also a Greek krater showing a tuna seller. Open daily 09:00–19:00 through October 📍€8
Osterio Magno — the Norman-era house said to be Roger II's, on Corso Ruggero. Stairs only 📍€2
The beach — long, sandy, free, right in the middle of town. Sea ~22°C: a last swim is genuinely possible on a sunny day 📍free
The medieval washhouse (lavatoio) — stone steps down to spring water where the town did its laundry for centuries. Hidden, two minutes off the main street 📍free
Porta Pescara & the old harbour — a stone arch framing the sea where the fishing boats still pull up. Best at golden hourfree

The Teatro Cicero and Roman road are closed Mondays — do those on another day; the Mandralisca stays open.

If you have spare time
  • Street food tour of Cefalù €49 A$83Two and a half hours, 10:00 start — pani ca meusa, panelle, arancina, sfincione, cannolo. Book direct with Sicilying. Monday to Saturday, so your Friday works.
  • Boat along the coast €39–60 A$66–102Cliffs and sea caves east of town, three hours with swim stops. Still running on your dates but it is the tail of the season — ask at the harbour when you arrive.
  • Castelbuono & the Madonie €2.90 + €6Trenitalia runs a combined train-and-bus ticket to Castelbuono Borgo — chestnut forests, a castle museum, and gelato flavoured with manna. A full day, so only if you skip something else.

With one night you get the Friday. La Rocca in the morning, the Duomo, lunch, a swim, then the train — that is a good day and enough of Cefalù. Save the excursions for Palermo.

Where to stay — 8 options by price
ℹ Just one night, so pick for convenience You arrive at 18:24 and leave the next evening. Somewhere in the old town or near the station beats somewhere with a pool you will never use.

Cheap · €70–92

  • Casa Roberto ~€70 Book9.6 "Exceptional", old town. Best value of the trip.
  • Hotel Mediterraneo 3★ €92 BookBreakfast included, 100 m from the station and outside the restricted-traffic zone — the easy-arrival option after a long travel day. 10 min walk to the old town.

Comfortable · €101–130

  • MiraMare Residence €101 Book9.6/10, location 10/10. A 40 m² apartment with a sea-view balcony inside the old town, three minutes from the Duomo, with a kitchen. Remarkable at this price.
  • Casanova Rooms €115 Book9.6/10 from 515 reviews with a shared Art Nouveau terrace. Free cancellation. Third floor, no lift.
  • B&B L&P €106 BookBreakfast included, old town, 8.9/10.

Treat yourself · €170–200

  • Hotel Riva del Sole €175 sea view BookDirectly on the seafront, sea-view room with balcony, breakfast in the garden, free parking, five minutes' walk to the old town. The best all-round splurge. Half board €265.
  • Salemare Rooms & Suites €195 Book9.6/10 from 727 reviews — the best-reviewed sea-view rooms actually inside the old town, steps from the beach. Breakfast included, free cancellation.

Note: Hotel Kalura is real but runs ~€305/night on your dates, not the €140 often quoted — out of range unless you want it badly. Hotel Baia del Capitano closes 26 Oct, mid-stay. City tax €2–2.50 per person per night on top, paid at the property.

Eat & drink

Cheap & essential

  • Ti Vitti €3–4 📍Cannoli piped full the moment you order, so the shell is still crisp. Non-negotiable.
  • Street kiosks €1.50–3.50Arancine (in Palermo they're feminine and round) €2.50–3.50, sfincione €1.50–2.50.

Dinner

  • La Brace €30–42pp 📍4.8/10 on Google from 885 reviews — the highest-rated place in Cefalù. Family-run since 1976, tiny, dinner only. Sicilian involtini (€14), swordfish rolls (€18). Closed Mondays. Booking required: +39 0921 423570.
  • Tinchitè Taverna €28–38pp 📍Two minutes from the Duomo. Order the pasta a "taianu" (€15) — Cefalù's own baked layered pasta with beef and aubergine, made nowhere else. Mostly walk-in; go at 19:30 or 21:00. The one open Mondays.
  • Ostaria del Duomo €38–52pp 📍Terrace directly on the cathedral square facing that Norman façade. Pasta con sarde €15. You're paying for the view — worth it once. Ask for the terrace: +39 0921 421838. Closed Mondays.
  • Cortile Pepe €60–70pp 📍Michelin-listed, tasting menus €75/€90. If you want one properly special dinner to end the trip, this is it. Closed Wednesdays.

You have one dinner here, on the Thursday. La Brace and Ostaria del Duomo are both open Thursdays — ring ahead, they are small. You arrive at 18:24, so book for 20:00 and drop your bag first.

kuhnmi / Wikimedia · CC BY 2.0 · more photos of Palermo

Palermo

23–27 Oct · 4 nights

Loud, layered and a bit dishevelled — Norman kings, Arab craftsmen and Spanish viceroys all left their mark and none of it was tidied up afterwards. This is the one proper city of the back half of the trip, and four nights is right: two for the mosaics, one for the sea, one for Monreale.

✓ Book this now: Rigoletto at the Teatro Massimo Verdi, in John Turturro’s production, on 23, 24 and 25 October while you are there. Ludovic Tézier sings the title role on the 25th — which is your free Sunday evening. Seats run €27–145; a good upper-tier seat is €40–60. On sale since December, so don’t leave it. teatromassimo.it
Walking map

One long straight street (Via Maqueda) crosses another (Corso Vittorio Emanuele) at the Quattro Canti. Almost everything is within ten minutes of that crossroads.

arrivesightsstayeat & beach3′ = minutes (by bike on Favignana)

Getting there — 23 Oct

Train from Cefalù €7.00–7.8043–65 min, around twenty a day, roughly hourly, last one about 22:00. Regionale is unreserved and fixed-price, so just turn up. Validate a paper ticket in the green machine on the platform or it is a fine; app tickets validate themselves. Arrives Palermo Centrale.

Where to stay — and which bit of the city
⚠ Don’t book the streets right around Palermo Centrale The cheapest listings cluster there and in Ballarò behind it, and local advice is consistent that the station quarter is not somewhere to be wandering after dark. Twelve minutes’ walk up the road is a different city.

Best areas: Quattro Canti / Via Maqueda is dead centre and an easy 12-minute flat walk from the station with bags. Kalsa is the same distance, better value and better for dinner — just stick to the Via Paternostro and Piazza Marina axis late at night. Politeama is the calmest and is where the Mondello and Monte Pellegrino buses start, but it is too far to walk from the station with luggage.

Good value · €93–114

  • Casa Busari (Cathedral quarter) €98 Book9.7 “Exceptional” from 506 reviews — the best score-to-price on this list. Large double, free cancellation. The pick.
  • Hotel Tonic 3★ (Politeama) €93 BookBreakfast included and free cancellation at this price, which is rare. Location scored 9.4. Right by the Mondello bus.
  • Ad Hoc Rooms (Kalsa) €114 Book9.0 from 766 reviews, location 9.8. Breakfast included and you pay at the property, nothing up front.

More comfort · €141–188

  • B&B Hotel Palermo Quattro Canti 3★ €141 BookLiterally on the Quattro Canti crossroads — the best-positioned address here. Lift, 24-hour desk, chain reliability. Location 9.6.
  • NH Palermo 4★ (Kalsa seafront) €172 BookA proper four-star with sea-facing rooms and a garden.
  • Hotel Politeama 4★ €188 Book8.9 from 2,186 reviews, location 9.7. On the square itself, and both the Mondello and Monte Pellegrino buses leave from next door.

The famous palazzo hotels — Piazza Borsa, Porta Felice, Massimo Plaza, Centrale Palace — are all running €232–309 a night on your dates, so €140–200 buys a good three or four star rather than a palace. Several mid-range rates showed only one or two rooms left.

The mosaics — the reason you came
Cappella Palatina & Palazzo dei Normanni — a royal chapel where Norman, Arab and Byzantine craftsmen all worked at once: gold mosaics under a carved wooden honeycomb ceiling. Arguably the most beautiful room in Italy. Last entry 15:45; Sunday mornings only book 📍€19
La Martorana — 12th-century Byzantine mosaics and the best art-per-euro in Sicily. Mornings only, roughly 10:00–13:00, closed Mondays — which is why it has to be Saturday. San Cataldo next door (€2.50) has three red domes 📍€2
Monreale — 6,500 m² of gold mosaic covering an entire cathedral, plus a cloister of 228 carved columns, no two alike. The greatest thing in Sicily. Bus 389 from Piazza Indipendenza, 35–45 min. Cathedral shuts 13:00–14:00; the cloister does not 📍~€6 + €8
Palermo Cathedral — nave free; the rooftop walk gets you out among the domes and battlements 📍free/€7
Capuchin Catacombs — 8,000 mummified Palermitans, still dressed, standing in corridors. Unforgettable and genuinely unsettling. Open 09:00–12:30 and 15:00–17:30 — go at 09:00 📍€5

Buy the €3.50 AMAT day ticket on the Monreale day — you will take four buses. Singles are €1.40 from a tabaccheria, €1.80 on board.

The rest of the city
Palazzo Abatellis — the regional gallery, in a Catalan-Gothic palace. The Triumph of Death fresco is worth the ticket alone. Closed Mondays; Sundays 09:00–13:00 only 📍€10
Palazzo Butera — a restored seafront palace turned private collection, old and contemporary hung together. Closed Mondays 📍€10
Orto Botanico — ten hectares of tropical planting five minutes from the station, and almost empty. October 09:00–18:00 📍€8
Castello della Zisa — a Fatimid-style pleasure palace built for a Norman king, with a muqarnas fountain room. Rarely crowded 📍€6
Ballarò and Mercato del Capo — the two working markets. Mornings, best before 11. Loud, alive, and prime pickpocket ground, so bag in front 📍free
Quattro Canti & Fontana Pretoria — the baroque crossroads and the fountain of naked marble gods the nuns objected to. Best at duskfree

Money-saver: the “Operart” combined ticket is €17 for the Teatro Massimo guided tour plus Palazzo Butera. The tour alone is €14, so Butera costs you €3 instead of €10.

Mondello & Monte Pellegrino — your Sunday

Sunday is Palermo’s worst day for monuments — Monreale shuts to visitors in the morning, the Martorana is mass only, Abatellis closes at one. So spend it outside. Both buses leave from the same square at Politeama, so it is one errand.

  • Bus 812 up Monte Pellegrino €1.40To the Santa Rosalia sanctuary, built into a cave on the mountain that closes off the bay. Goethe called this headland the most beautiful promontory in the world.
  • Bus 806 to Mondello €1.40 ~35 minA curve of white sand under the mountain, with a Liberty-style bathing pavilion standing on stilts out in the bay. Sea is ~22°C in late October — genuinely swimmable. 📍
  • Get the €3.50 day ticketTwo buses out and two back — it pays for itself, and saves queuing at a tabaccheria each time.

Two things to know. The 806 runs a winter timetable by late October — roughly every 20 minutes rather than every 10, and locals report longer waits, so don’t cut it fine. And the paid lidos are winding down; who is even running the beach concession is tied up in a legal dispute this year. The free public beach is unaffected, which is all you need. The famous Charleston restaurant left the pavilion back in 2010, so don’t go looking for it.

Evenings
  • Rigoletto at the Teatro Massimo €27–14523, 24 and 25 October. Europe’s third-largest opera house, and the staircase from the end of The Godfather Part III. Tézier sings on the 25th. Book
  • Teatro Massimo guided tour €14Forty minutes, daily, last tour 18:20 — if you would rather see it in daylight than sit through Verdi.
  • Opera dei Pupi — Sicilian puppet theatre €10Museo Pasqualino in the Kalsa: museum plus a show, Tue–Sat at 17:00, Mondays at 11:00. Armoured knights, real swordfights, entirely serious about it. UNESCO-listed as living heritage.
  • Vucciria after dark freeThe old market square turns into an open-air drinking and street-food scene until very late. Safe because it is busy — but taxi the last stretch home rather than walking empty streets at 2am.
Eat

Cheap and essential

  • Antica Focacceria San Francesco €10–20pp 📍The historic address for pane ca meusa — spleen in a bun — plus arancine and sarde a beccafico. Touristy now, but it is the real place and the only reliable sit-down for spleen. Open daily.
  • Trattoria Al Ferro di Cavallo €10–20pp 📍Palermitan home cooking near Quattro Canti, huge portions, walls you are invited to write on. No bookings, expect a queue. Closed Sunday; Mon–Tue lunch only.

Dinner

  • Trattoria Ai Cascinari €20–30pp 📍4.6 from 2,565 reviews — the local favourite and the best-rated of the lot. Closed Monday and Tuesday, so on your dates that means Friday, Saturday or Sunday. Book.
  • Bisso Bistrot €20–30pp 📍On Quattro Canti itself. Old osteria recipes off a chalkboard, bought at the market that morning, buzzy and cheap for what it is. Open daily.
  • Osteria Ballarò €30–50pp 📍In the stables of a palazzo. Pasta con le sarde, spaghetti vongole, and a street-food tasting platter if you want it all at once. Open daily, but book.
Moving on — 27 Oct to Trapani
⚠ Take the bus, not the train The direct Palermo–Trapani railway has been closed since 2013 and is not reopening this decade. What is left loops via Marsala and takes four to five and a half hours with a change. The bus takes two.

Segesta coach to Trapani €9.60Two hours, direct, eight a day on weekdays. Leaves from Piazzetta Cairoli, the terminus immediately behind Palermo Centrale — two minutes from the platforms. It drops you at Trapani port, which is exactly where the Favignana hydrofoils leave from.

Left luggage if you need it €3.50–6Radical Storage or Bounce near Palermo Centrale are about €3.90 a bag per day; the official KiPoint inside the station is €6 for five hours and shuts at 20:00.

Maxdonati / Wikimedia · CC BY 3.0 · more photos of Favignana

Favignana

27–31 Oct · 4 nights

A flat, butterfly-shaped island off the west coast where the old tuff quarries have flooded and turned into swimming holes with sheer cut-stone walls. Everyone gets about by bicycle. After three weeks of ruins and cities, this is the trip letting go.

⚠ Book Favignana before anything else You are arriving in the last week of the season. The island has 160 places bookable for your dates and is very much open — but the proper hotels are closing (Hotel Aegusa stops selling on 27 October, the day you arrive), so the good apartments and B&Bs will go first. Book on a free-cancellation rate.
Map

Flat across the east, hilly in the west. Distances are from the town; everything east is an easy ride on any bike.

arrivesightsstayeat & beach3′ = minutes (by bike on Favignana)

Getting there — 27 Oct
ℹ There is no boat from Palermo Not in any season — the Egadi hydrofoils all leave from Trapani. The Palermo boat people think of goes to Ustica, which is a different island entirely.

1 · Coach to Trapani ~€10Segesta Autolinee, two hours, roughly hourly from 06:00, from the coach terminus behind Palermo Centrale. Take the bus, not the train — the direct railway has been shut since 2013 and what is left loops via Marsala in over three hours. The coach also puts you at Trapani port, 50 m from the hydrofoil.

2 · Hydrofoil to Favignana ~€12Thirty to forty minutes, around a dozen a day in low season. Liberty Lines — book online or at the port office, and be there fifteen minutes early.

⚠ Luggage limit on the hydrofoil One free bag, 10 kg and 60×40×20 cm. A normal suitcase needs a paid baggage ticket — budget a few euro and don’t be surprised at the desk. Bicycles are not carried, which is fine: you hire one on the island for €5.
Where to stay — stay in the town
ℹ In low season, walking distance matters more than a view Everything still trading in late October — the open trattorias, the bakery, the pharmacy, the bike shops, the quay, the museum — sits between the port and Piazza Madrice. It is dark by 17:45, so a place out in the countryside means cycling home in the dark past nothing. Aim for five minutes’ walk of Piazza Madrice.

Good value · €80–107

  • Casa Maja rooms & suites €80 Book8.8 from 363 reviews, 200 m from the centre, superior double with a balcony. The value pick.
  • Dimora La Torre €84 BookFifty metres from the centre — you cannot be more central. Free cancellation.
  • Egusa73 €100 Book9.2 from 440 reviews, king room, free cancellation, 150 m in.
  • La Casa dell’Arancio €107 Book direct9.0 from 375 reviews, a 35 m² suite with breakfast. Their own site lists a “bassissima stagione” rate of €95 including breakfast for 18 Oct–2 Nov, so booking direct beats the platforms.

Nicer · €126–168

  • Mazzini Accommodation €126 Book9.5 from 440 reviews — the strongest review profile on the island, breakfast included, and forty metres from the centre. If you want to be sure, this is it.
  • Albergo Egadi €168 Book9.5, breakfast, free cancellation. One guide lists it as shut in late October but it was live and bookable for your dates — confirm with them directly before relying on it.

Cheaper still if you don’t mind basic: Affittacamere Il Tufo on Via Marconi runs about €43–65 a night, and B&B Favignana on Via Roma publishes €60 with breakfast for the 1 Oct–15 Nov window.

The island by bike

Nineteen square kilometres, about nine across, flat except for one hill, and around 20 km of bike paths. Hire on arrival — the shops publish an explicit October–December rate, so they are open.

Bike hire — includes basket, lock, lights and roadside help. Quotes vary by shop: €5–8 for a standard bike, €10–20 for an e-bike, €25–50 for a scooter. Noleggio Isidoro on Via Mazzini has traded since 1970 and publishes low-season hours, so is the safest first call; Info Point at the port will deliver to your door. Book a day ahead by WhatsApp rather than turning up€5–8/day
Cala Rossa — the famous one, 3.7 km and about twenty flat minutes, with the last 700 m on white unpaved road. Not a beach: terraces of cut tuff dropping into turquoise, an old quarry the sea moved into. Named for the sea battle that ended the First Punic War, fought just offshore in 241 BC. Best light late afternoon 📍free
Bue Marino — 4 km, next along. Steps cut into the rock and slides straight into deep water — the bottom drops away immediately, so not one for a tentative swimmer. Best snorkelling on the island 📍free
Cala Azzurra — 4 km. White sand with a pink tint, shallow and sheltered: the easiest swim on the island. Expect banks of dried seagrass on the rocks by late October — that is normal here in winter 📍free
Lido Burrone — only 1.8 km, the closest and the island’s only proper sandy beach. The lido and its bar will be shut; the sand is very much open 📍free
Monte Santa Caterina — 314 m, the island high point, with a derelict Norman-then-Bourbon-prison fort on top. Cycle halfway, then steps. The best view in the Egadi: the whole butterfly, Levanzo, and Trapani across the water. Go before 15:30 — sunset is 17:15 📍free

The one local trick worth knowing: every cove here has a wind it works in and a wind it does not. If the maestrale is blowing from the north-west, go to the sheltered south and east side — Cala Azzurra, Lido Burrone. In a southerly, Cala Rossa comes into its own. Ask at your B&B in the morning which side is calm; it makes more difference than the forecast temperature.

The eastern coves make one easy flat loop in a morning. Nothing is open at any of them — no bar, no kiosk, no toilets — so carry water, lunch and a towel from town. West of the hill it gets properly hilly: Cala Rotonda (5 km, with the Arco di Ulisse rock arch) and Punta Sottile lighthouse (7 km, the sunset point looking out to Marettimo) are both worth it, but that is where an e-bike earns its money. Watch the clock coming back from Punta Sottile — it is dark at 17:15 and there is no lighting.

Sights & the Levanzo day trip
Ex Stabilimento Florio — the old tuna cannery, and the best thing on the island. This was one of the great tuna fisheries of the Mediterranean; the museum covers the mattanza, the Florio family, and bronze rams recovered from the 241 BC battle. An English guided tour is included. €12 combined with Palazzo Florio 📍€10
Giardino dell’Impossibile — four hectares planted down inside abandoned tuff quarries, ~500 species among tunnels and sunken walls, with sculpture among the planting. About 90 minutes with the audio guide. Season ends 2 November, so you just catch it — go in the morning slot (09:30–13:30), and book ahead on +39 380 152 7808€15
Levanzo — ten minutes by hydrofoil, seven sailings a day. One whitewashed harbour village and some coves. The reason to go is the Grotta del Genovese and its 10,000-year-old cave paintings 📍~€6–10
Grotta del Genovese — €44 with boat or off-road transport and a guide, or €22 if you walk in yourself (4 km each way, about an hour, and there is nothing to hire on Levanzo). Booking is compulsory, 48 hours minimum, mornings only — +39 331 133 0259, WhatsApp works€22/44
⚠ Two things to ring ahead about The Florio museum’s autumn hours are not published — the times online are the summer ones and it likely closes early November (+39 338 536 5899). And the Grotta del Genovese publishes no season at all. Both are worth a WhatsApp before you go, because they are two of the three best things to do here.
Eat — tuna, and more tuna

This was a tuna island for a thousand years and the food still says so. Look for tonno rosso grilled or as tartare, bottarga grated over spaghetti, busiate with pesto alla trapanese (almonds, tomato, basil), and cous cous di pesce — the Trapanese inheritance from North Africa, and exactly what the surviving trattorias cook in autumn.

  • SottoSale & La BettolaThe two named as reliably open in low season, serving fish couscous by the fireplace — which tells you what late October here is like.
  • Quello che c’è… c’è €25–35pp4.2 from over 3,000 reviews, and named by an off-season guide as staying open.
  • Trattoria La Pinnata / Dispensa Sicana €25–35ppBoth central and well rated. Dispensa Sicana is closed Tuesdays.
  • Er Paninaro a few €On the waterfront, and reckoned to do the best tuna sandwich on the island, plus pane cunzato and proper granita. Exactly what you want for a day on the bike.
  • La Kebbaberia di Tonno cheapTuna kebab, tuna burgers, tuna sausage. Sounds like a gimmick, is genuinely good, and is the most Favignana thing you can eat for under a tenner.
  • Santi e Marinai €Near the port, 4.7 from nearly a thousand reviews. Fish sandwiches and arancini made fresh each morning.
  • Panificio CostanzaThe bakery, open year-round. Somewhere to start the day and stock the pannier.

Expect roughly a third to a half of the summer’s restaurants trading — enough for four nights, not enough to be fussy. The genuinely dead months are November to March, which you miss.

What to expect, honestly

Sea 21°C, air 22–23°C, dark at 17:45. The water is warmer than Sydney is for most of the year, so swimming is genuinely on — brisk for two minutes then fine. Go at midday; the limit is wind, not water.

  • You will have Cala Rossa to yourself. That is the trade.
  • Boat trips round the island have probably stopped. The coves circuit is only €25 for six hours and would be the highlight if it ran — but every operator lists the season as May to October and you are at the very end of it. Email booking@infopointfavignana.com before you go. If scheduled trips are off, ask about a private gozzo with a local fisherman, which is often arrangeable on the day if the sea is flat.
  • No lidos, sunbeds or beach bars. Bring a towel.
  • Roughly a one-in-three chance of rain on any given day, and wind matters more than rain here. If a maestrale is blowing, use the sheltered south and east coves.
  • Short days and quiet evenings. This is a working Sicilian fishing town in its off-season, not a resort.
  • There is an island bus (€1.10 a ride, €3.60 a day) on three routes, but it does not reach Cala Rossa or Bue Marino and its off-season timetable is anyone’s guess. Hire the bike.
ℹ Four nights is generous for this island in late October Three full days is a lot of a quiet place. Make one of them Levanzo and it works nicely. If it starts to feel long, the alternative is to drop a night and spend it in Trapani or Erice on the way back — both trade year-round, and it takes the pressure off the 31st.

Back to Rome & home

31 Oct – 1 Nov

One night of buffer before an international flight, and the leg with the most moving parts. Worth reading properly — there is one thing here that would have caught you out.

⚠ There is no flight from Trapani to Rome on Saturday 31 October The winter Trapani–Rome service runs roughly Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday — one flight a day, and not Saturdays. Checked directly: the 31st comes back empty, while the 30th and the 2nd both have flights. So you go back through Palermo, which is straightforward and has seventeen flights to Rome that day.
The route — Saturday 31 Oct

~08:30 · Hydrofoil Favignana → Trapani ~€12Thirty to forty minutes. Take a morning sailing, not a later one — if it is cancelled for weather you want the rest of the day to recover.

~10:00 · Coach Trapani → Palermo airport ~€10Segesta run it direct in about an hour and ten, roughly hourly, every day including holidays — and it leaves from the same quay the hydrofoil arrives at. No trek across town.

Afternoon · Palermo → Rome €22–49Seventeen nonstops that day, about an hour and a quarter. An afternoon departure (around 15:00) leaves a deliberate few hours of slack at the airport — enough to absorb one cancelled boat and still fly.

Into Rome €14Leonardo Express from Fiumicino to Termini, 32 min, every 15 minutes.

All in, about €60 a head and you are in Rome by late afternoon with the evening free. Last carbonara, and repack.

If you would rather not risk it
  • Leave a day early €33Friday 30 Oct has a direct Trapani–Rome flight at 15:10. Removes the boat risk and the Palermo transfer entirely, at the cost of one Favignana night.
  • Night in TrapaniCross on the 30th, sleep in Trapani or up in Erice, then take a morning flight from Palermo on the 31st. Erice is a walled medieval town on a mountain and a genuinely good last stop.

Whatever you choose: do not book a 31 Oct flight leaving before about 1pm that depends on a same-morning hydrofoil.

1 Nov — departure day
  • It is All Saints’ Day, a Sunday. The Vatican is closed; state museums including the Colosseum are free that morning if you have hours to spare — though busy.
  • Leonardo Express to FCO €14, every 15 min, 32 min. Allow three hours before an international flight.
  • Or the fixed €55 taxi — white “Roma Capitale” cars only.
  • Public transport runs a Sunday timetable, so leave a little extra margin.

Two habits worth having

  • Say buongiorno walking into any shop or bar, and arrivederci leaving. Not doing it reads as rude.
  • Coffee standing at the bar is €1.20–1.50 and sitting down is triple. Order, drink it there, pay on the way out.
  • A coperto of €1–3 on the bill is a cover charge, not a scam and not a tip.
  • Ask for “un caffè” and you get an espresso. Asking for a latte gets you a glass of milk.

What’s shut, and when

The single most common way to waste a morning in Italy is turning up on the wrong day. Your itinerary already dodges most of these — this is the check-before-you-walk list.

Monday
  • Borghese Gallery, Rome — closed
  • Villa Jovis and Certosa, Capri — closed
  • La Martorana, Palermo — closed
  • Teatro Cicero & Roman road, Cefalù — closed
  • Cefalù restaurants — La Brace, Ostaria del Duomo and La Botte all shut. Tinchitè is open.
  • Ostia Antica — closed
Tuesday
  • MANN museum, Naples — closed
  • Capri restaurants — the commonest closing day; Lo Sfizio shut, Al Grottino possibly. Il Solitario and Le Arcate open.
Wednesday
  • Catacombs of San Callisto, Rome — closed (use San Sebastiano)
  • Cortile Pepe, Cefalù — closed
  • Papal audience morning — St Peter’s Square closed off, Vatican area heaving
Sunday
  • Vatican Museums — closed all day
  • Monreale — cathedral shut to tourists in the morning
  • Cefalù street food tour — does not run
  • Calabrian regional buses — no service at all
  • Shops and small towns generally quiet; trains on reduced timetables
Every day, midday
  • Southern Italy shuts 13:00–15:30ish. Shops, some churches, most museums in smaller towns.
  • San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome — 12:45–14:30
  • Capuchin Catacombs, Palermo — 12:30–15:00
  • Monreale cathedral — 13:00–14:00 (the cloister stays open)
  • Dinner rarely starts before 20:00. Turning up at 19:00 means eating alone.
Last entries that catch people out
  • La Rocca, Cefalù — last entry 17:30, and enforced
  • Pompeii — last entry 17:30 (site closes 19:30)
  • Cappella Palatina, Palermo — last entry 15:45
  • Villa Jovis, Capri — from 16 Oct it closes 16:00, last entry 15:30
  • Blue Grotto — last entry ~15:30, and it shuts without warning in swell
✓ Your dates already avoid the worst of it Palermo city day is Tuesday so the Martorana is open; the Monreale day is Monday when it’s shut anyway; and Cefalù’s Monday closures are covered by Tinchitè.

Money

  • Best setup: Up Bank debit (0% foreign fees, free overseas ATMs) as your main card, Wise as backup. Order both now — 1–2 weeks to arrive.
  • ATMs: use bank machines (Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, BNL). Never Euronet — they're everywhere in tourist areas and they're the expensive ones.
  • The one rule: when the ATM offers to "convert to AUD", always say no and choose euros. That offer costs you 5–10%.
  • Cash: keep €200–300 on you. Needed for SITA buses, tabacchi, markets, small trattorias, porters, and the city tax at check-out.
  • Tipping: not expected. The €1–3 "coperto" on your bill is a cover charge, not a scam. Round up or leave €2–5 if you had a lovely time.
  • Daily food: ~€26 eating cheap, €42–57 with a trattoria dinner. Lunch is 30–40% cheaper than the same meal at night.

Phone & data

  • Airalo Eurolink eSIM, 50GB / 90 days ≈ A$148 — one plan, whole trip, connects automatically when you land. Install before you fly.
  • Don't use Australian roaming: $5–10 a day works out to A$225–450.
  • Before you go, on wifi: download offline Google Maps for Rome, Naples/Amalfi, Calabria and Sicily, plus the Google Translate Italian pack. Offline maps use no data and work with GPS.
  • Apps to install: Trenitalia · Italo · Ferryhopper · Moovit · Unico Campania · FreeNow · TheFork.
  • Power: Australian plugs don't fit. Bring two Type C "Europlug" adapters. Same voltage, so no converter needed.

Safety & scams

These are safe places. The risk is petty theft, not anything worse, and the whole defence is keeping your bag in front of you in crowds. Official advice: Smartraveller.

  • Where to concentrate: Termini station, Metro Line A, bus 64, the Trevi crush; and in Naples, Garibaldi station and the Circumvesuviana train — that line has a real reputation. Bag zipped, in front, phone away from the doors.
  • Two scams to know: anyone tying a "free" bracelet on your wrist, and anyone with a petition clipboard. Both are distractions. Don't stop, don't take anything offered.
  • Taxis: official white cars only, meter on Tariff 1, or use the FreeNow app. From FCO it's a fixed €55 — check the door says "Roma Capitale".
  • Validate paper train and bus tickets in the little machines before boarding. €100 fine, and they do check.
  • Passport: carry it on Pompeii day (your ticket is named). Otherwise a photo on your phone and the real one in the room safe.

Packing

  • A 40–50L backpack or small soft case — not a big roller. Positano is stairs, Capri is stairs, and Italian stations love a broken lift. Ferries charge extra for big bags.
  • Pack a week of clothes and do laundry mid-trip — a self-service lavanderia is €14–20 wash and dry, or ask your hotel.
  • Layers: t-shirts, a light jumper, a packable rain jacket. Evenings drop to 12–15°C by late October.
  • Shoes matter here. Pompeii is uneven stone, La Rocca requires closed shoes, and Positano is a staircase. One pair of real walking shoes.
  • Swimmers and a quick-dry towel — the sea is 21–22°C the whole way down and the beaches are empty.
  • Hat, sunscreen, small umbrella, a scarf (doubles as shoulder cover in churches), two Type C adapters, and a refillable bottle — Rome has 2,500 free drinking fountains.

If you spend the extra, spend it here

  • Stromboli by night, from Tropea €70Lava running into the sea after dark, on one of the last boats of the season. Nothing else on this trip is like it.
  • Rigoletto at the Teatro Massimo €40–60Verdi in Europe's third-largest opera house, with a world-class Rigoletto, on your free Sunday night in Palermo.
  • Cooking class in Sorrento €95–125Your extra Sorrento day makes room for it. You come home able to make it again.
  • Grotta del Genovese, Levanzo €44Ten-thousand-year-old cave paintings reached by boat or 4x4. The guided version is worth it over walking 4 km each way.
  • Testaccio food tour, Rome €79Best possible first-week orientation, and you eat better all trip for having done it.
  • An e-bike on Favignana +€10/dayUnlocks the hilly western half — Cala Rotonda and the lighthouse at Punta Sottile.
  • Three very good dinners €35–50ppRoscioli in Rome, Ai Cascinari in Palermo, and whatever is open and full of locals on Favignana.
